consistency_with_frozen_trigger.residual_audit_finding: Fully consistent with, and further corroborates, the frozen ABSENT trigger. Zero of the 29 residual claims were classified VALID_A001_SUPPORT (0/29). 19/29 are explicit opposition/invalidation of the easing thesis (rate headwinds, rate repricing pressure, explicit rising-rate statements, explicit negations of the case for cuts), 8/29 are generic, non-directional rate-sensitivity commentary with no cut/easing assertion, 1/29 is a conditional mention-only hedge, and 1/29 is a genuinely mixed/ambiguous claim that itself only cites an 'unchanged rates' (not a cut) counterpoint against a stated hawkish base case. Nothing in this row-level inspection contradicts or weakens the frozen trigger; if anything, it independently reconfirms that no meaningful current Rate Cut Cycle evidence exists in this run's persisted corpus.

release_validation_gate.reason: A systematic residual false-positive mechanism remains: 19/29 (65.5%) residual claims are GENERIC_MACRO_OVERMATCH -- generic rate-headwind/rate-repricing/rate-pressure language describing an adverse (anti-easing) or non-directional rate environment, none of which contains the specific phrasings the Step-7A veto's enumerated pattern list covers. A further 8 claims show explicit opposition (rates rising, case for cuts reduced, reversal from easing expectations) that also escape the current veto, plus one identified, concrete phrasing gap ('pricing a hike' without the word 'rate' immediately adjacent). Zero of the 29 are genuine positive A001 evidence. A fresh live QQQ run against the same/similar market conditions would very likely re-create a comparable pool of topically-matched-but-non-directional or opposing evidence, since the underlying LLM mapping tendency (topic-match regardless of direction) that Step 7A only partially addressed is still intact for this broader class of phrasing. This is exactly the 'repeatable semantic gap' / 'live run would predictably re-create unsupported A001 evidence' condition this task's own gate defines as NOT ready.

second_remediation_recommendation.residual_mechanism: GENERIC_MACRO_OVERMATCH (dominant, 19/29): generic 'rate headwind'/'rate repricing'/'rate pressure' language with no explicit cut/easing assertion, and no explicit hike/hawkish/rising-yield phrasing either -- an intermediate class the Step-7A blocklist does not cover. Plus RATE_DIRECTION_MISREAD (3), NEGATION_MISREAD (3), and MODALITY_MISREAD (2): claims with an explicit rising-rate or negated-easing assertion, and one POST_DECISION_VETO_INCOMPLETE case ('pricing a hike' without the word 'rate' immediately adjacent, an identified gap in the existing veto's phrase coverage).
